title: Tiling a Rectangle by a Grid
content: The module docstring frames the open question. The parent file proved both sides of the concrete Green identity are additive under a single cut and packaged the vertical direction as a gluing capstone. Two steps remained: the horizontal companion capstone, and a genuinely two-dimensional grid statement. This file supplies both, taking the 2×2 grid as the prototype from which an arbitrary m×n tiling follows by iteration.
mathContext: Green's theorem on a region $R$ tiled by cells $R = \bigcup_{i,j} R_{ij}$ equals the sum $\sum_{i,j}$ of the cellwise identities; every interior edge is traversed once in each direction, so $\oint_{\partial R_{ij}}$ along it cancels with the neighbor's.

title: Composing on the Parent File
content: The file imports Proofs.GreensTheoremOQ01OQ03 and opens both GreensTheoremOQ01 (for rectLineIntegral, rectDoubleIntegral, area_double_integral) and GreensTheoremOQ01OQ03 (for the single-cut split lemmas and the vertical capstone). No new analytic machinery is introduced; everything is built by composing already-verified lemmas, which is why the file stays axiom-free.
mathContext: All content reduces to the parent's $\texttt{rectLineIntegral}$, $\texttt{rectDoubleIntegral}$, and the split lemmas $\texttt{rectLineIntegral\_hsplit}$, $\texttt{rectDoubleIntegral\_hsplit}$.

title: Horizontal Gluing Capstone
content: greens_additive_horizontal is the mirror of the parent's greens_additive_vertical. Given Green's identity on a bottom cell [a,b]×[c,g] and a top cell [a,b]×[g,d], it follows on [a,b]×[c,d]. The proof is a single rewrite: undo the additivity of both sides across y=g via rectLineIntegral_hsplit and rectDoubleIntegral_hsplit, then substitute the two cell identities hB and hT. The shared horizontal edge y=g cancels by orientation with no extra hypothesis.
mathContext: $\oint_{\partial([a,b]\times[c,d])} = \oint_{\partial([a,b]\times[c,g])} + \oint_{\partial([a,b]\times[g,d])}$ because the interior segment $y=g$ is traversed right-to-left for the bottom cell and left-to-right for the top cell.

title: Integrability Hypotheses for the Glue
content: The four IntervalIntegrable hypotheses on Q(b,·) and Q(a,·) over [c,g] and [g,d], plus two on the inner-integral fiber ∫ₐᵇ F(x,·), are exactly what intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals consumes to merge ∫_c^g + ∫_g^d into ∫_c^d. Without integrability on each subinterval the additivity of the integral can fail, so these conditions are not bureaucratic — they are the precise analytic content that makes the glue valid.
mathContext: $\int_c^g h + \int_g^d h = \int_c^d h$ requires $h$ interval-integrable on $[c,g]$ and $[g,d]$; here $h(y)=Q(\cdot,y)$ on the edges and $h(y)=\int_a^b F(x,y)\,dx$ for the double integral.

title: The 2×2 Grid Capstone
content: greens_grid_2x2 is the first genuinely two-dimensional tiling in the gallery. Cutting [a,b]×[c,d] at x=e and y=g yields four cells BL, BR, TL, TR. The proof is pure composition: greens_additive_vertical glues BL+BR into the bottom strip [a,b]×[c,g] and TL+TR into the top strip [a,b]×[g,d] (handling the vertical edge x=e twice), then greens_additive_horizontal glues the two strips across y=g. Both interior edges cancel automatically; no cancellation input is needed beyond the integrability data.
mathContext: $\partial(\text{BL})+\partial(\text{BR})+\partial(\text{TL})+\partial(\text{TR}) = \partial([a,b]\times[c,d])$: the vertical edge $x=e$ cancels within each row, the horizontal edge $y=g$ cancels between rows.
prerequisites: Green's theorem additive under single cut

title: Row-First, Then Across Rows
content: The gluing order matters for keeping each cancellation local. By first assembling the two horizontal strips (vertical glue along x=e within each row) and only then gluing the strips across y=g, every interior segment is eliminated in exactly one gluing step. The shared hypotheses (e.g. P(·,g) over the two columns, and the outer F-integral over [a,b]) are reused across steps, which is why the long hypothesis list collapses to three applications of the parent capstones.

title: Concrete Area Sanity Check
content: area_grid_2x2_unit_square verifies the abstract grid identity on a fully concrete case: the area of [0,1]² computed as the double integral of 1 equals the sum of its four quarter-cells. Each quarter-cell has area ¼; rewriting all five double integrals through area_double_integral reduces the goal to ¼+¼+¼+¼=1, closed by ring. This guards against vacuous or sign-confused statements of the grid lemma.

title: Axiom Audit
content: The closing #print axioms commands confirm greens_additive_horizontal and greens_grid_2x2 depend only on the standard foundational axioms propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound — no Lean.ofReduceBool (so no native_decide) and no sorryAx. This certifies the entry as genuinely verified rather than axiomatized: the result is fully machine-checked.
mathContext: $\#\text{print axioms} \Rightarrow \{\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound}\}$ only — the ordinary foundations, none of which count as assumptions.
